title: Embedding burst QoS: tiered queueing, headroom reservations, and predictive autoscaling
creator: Ravi Patel
description: High-level: Production embeddings workloads show frequent short-duration burst traffic that causes queue pileups, increased p99 latency, and noisy neighbor effects across tenants. This ticket implements a QoS-oriented shaping layer for the embeddings router: tiered queues (premium/standard/best-effort), headroom reservation for high-value customers, and predictive autoscaling signals to pre-warm pools before bursts. Goal: bring 99th percentile end-to-end embedding latency under 120ms for premium tier during 95th-percentile bursts while keeping overall cost within current budget envelopes.
background: Over the last two months we've observed three incidents where medium-duration burst traffic doubled embedding queue depth and forced eviction of cached KV entries. Existing autoscaler reacts to sustained queue length, but bursts are too short for reactive scaling. Benchmarks: internal loadtests show 3x short bursts (30s) cause p99 to increase from 85ms to 420ms for standard tenants. Current rate-limiter is token-bucket only and does not preserve headroom for high-value customers.
proposed_design: 1) Tiered in-memory queue per router worker: small SPSC ring buffers for premium, larger shared queues for standard, and background FIFO for best-effort. 2) Headroom reservation: maintain a small number of reserved slots on each worker for premium tokens (configurable per-tenant). 3) Burst predictor: lightweight sliding-window model in the control plane that emits 'pre-warm' signals when a tenant's request rate slope exceeds threshold. 4) Autoscaler integration: accept predictive signal to pre-allocate fractional units (20-40%) ahead of predicted burst. 5) Token-aware rate limits: per-tenant rate windows that consider average token length to avoid unfairness when some tenants send much longer sequences. 6) Observability: add per-queue metrics, reserved-slot utilization, predictor confidence, and surge-scaling events to Console dashboards and alerting rules.
tradeoffs: Pre-warming increases short-term cost; we mitigate with tight pre-warm budgets and rollback on low predictor precision.
Tiered queues add scheduling complexity and slightly more memory per worker but reduce p99 dramatically for premium tenants.
Predictor may have false positives; design includes a confidence cutoff and max pre-warm cap to limit waste.
Reserved headroom may reduce peak throughput available to standard tenants; goal is configurable percent (default 10%) per worker to balance fairness.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end p99 embedding latency <= 120ms for premium tier during 95th-percentile historical burst profiles (verified by synthetic replay).
No more than 15% increase in total GPU-hours attributable to pre-warm activity over a 30-day rolling window at default config.
Per-queue metrics emitted to Console with retention 30d and dashboard tile created (embeddings.qos.*).
Fallback: when predictor unavailable, router falls back to reactive autoscaler and tiered queue still enforces reservations.
Load-test PRs and simulation results reviewed and approved by eng+pm; relevant PRs merged.
progress_updates: 2026-02-26: Spike completed with microbench harness to validate per-worker ring buffer performance (perf notes in doc). Premium queue enqueue/dequeue latency measured < 2us under contention - R.Patel.
2026-03-02: Prototype predictor implemented in control plane as Holt-Winters-like slope detector. In local sim it catches 72% of bursts with 18% false positive rate - A.Mehtha.

2026-03-05: Design review with infra and finance. Infra requests hard cap on pre-warm instances per region; Finance requested telemetry to attribute cost to pre-warms - action: add cost tags to pre-warm pools.
2026-03-08: Integration branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/routers/pull/1423; includes queue primitives and reservation API. Perf tests running in CI.

2026-03-10: CTO requested gate: ensure security_review_required for tenant isolation; product agreed review not required for first iteration (security_review_required=false) but will be revisited before private deployment.
qa_plan: 1) Replay of 50 historical burst traces against staging with and without QoS layer. 2) Synthetic stress ramps to validate pre-warm efficacy and ensure no cascading failures. 3) Chaos test: kill pre-warmed instances during a burst to verify rollback/fallback behavior. 4) Compare billing attribution metrics between baseline and QoS-enabled runs.
rollout_plan: canary: enable QoS and predictor for 2% of premium tenants in us-west for 48 hours, monitor p99 and pre-warm cost.
gradual: 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% of premium tenants over 2 weeks with rollback windows and auto-disable on cost/latency regressions.
global: enable tiered queues for standard tenants after premium rollout is stable; best-effort remains default off until month-end review.
